To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Machine learning enabled identification of structural phase transitions and associated phase diagrams in ferroelectric materials based on experimental data.
machine learning of dynamic responses of materials enables the determination of structural phase transition boundaries in relaxor ferrielectrics.

1) machine learning is a promising method to identify phase transitions in ferromagnets and ferroelectrics; 2) machine learning of dynamic responses of ferroelectric materials allows for determination of structural phase transition; 3) machine learning of the collective dynamics of ferroelectrics allows determination of structural transitions in nanometer scale volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of machine learning approaches for the analysis of multidimensional experimental data.
the development of a machine learning based approach to the determination of structural phase transition boundaries in ferroelectric systems.
the development of a new method for the identification of structural phase transitions based on piezoelectric measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
machine learning approaches are suitable to determine phase transitions, and the phase diagram of a material, in a statistically significant, robust, and general manner.
machine learning of collective dynamics allows for the determination of structural phase transition in relaxor ferromagnets.
machine learning is a powerful tool to identify material phase transitions, and that the presented approach is a general one that is applicable to a wide range of systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to identify a structural phase transition based on experimental data, without the use of any theoretical model, and with a minimal amount of data.
machine learning is a powerful approach for the identification of structural phase transitions, and can be used for the analysis of data from multiple experimental realizations.
we have developed and demonstrated a new approach to the determination of the phase diagram of ferroelectrics using machine learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
machine learning can be used to identify the presence of phase transitions in materials, even if the order parameter is not known.
the machine learning approach allows the identification of the phase transition in the relaxor without any a priori knowledge on the order parameter.
the collective dynamic behavior of a system can be used as a probe for phase transitions, even in cases where the microscopic order parameter is not known.
